**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Include the M2 client support before enabling this journey**

When `run <dir> nc m2` packages this commit's own tree, the first alert click cannot reach `path`: `src/notifications/contract.ts` still declares only `CLIENT_GROUPS = ['okr']`, and the desktop proxy in `src/shell/policy.cjs` also drops `X-OKR-Notification-Groups`, while every row exercised here belongs to `flow` or `replies`. The entry route therefore resolves as `update_required` and this URL assertion times out, so the newly advertised test does not pass alone until the client and proxy changes are included.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L150-L156](https://github.com/txehq/txe/blob/cdc736305680f31259ad9eb0390a65d5a51c12e9/AGENTS.md#L150-L156)

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Restore the activated source groups after the test**

After this spec runs on a kept database, `flow` and `replies` remain active because no failure-safe teardown reverses this update. Running an existing NC spec that calls `ncReal.activateOkrGroup()` afterward, such as `notifications-ui.real.spec.ts`, then fails its exact `flow=false,okr=true,replies=false` precondition before testing anything; restore these shared rows in `afterAll`, including on failure, as the existing M2 real-stack spec does.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Explicitly clear the recording notifier for the OS run**

When the operator already has `OKR_DESKTOP_NOTIFY_LOG` exported, assigning `notify=()` merely omits a command-line override; `env` and then `desktopTarget` still inherit the variable from the caller. The `os` spec consequently stops at its assertion that the variable is unset instead of exercising macOS. Pass an explicit empty value or remove the variable from the environment for this branch.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Retire the warm-up alert before restarting**

When macOS drops the first notification while displaying the permission prompt—the case this warm-up explicitly permits—`alert-not-presented` or `alert-not-shown` is not acknowledged, so closing here leaves `warm.candidate` pending. After the fresh launch acquires the lease, that warm-up can be presented before the counted candidate; both banners have the same text, so the person can click the wrong one and the test times out without proving the advertised single-notification journey. Cancel, read, or otherwise finish the warm-up candidate before reopening the app.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Restore source-group activation after the OS spec**

When `run <dir> nc os` is followed by the ordinary `run <dir> nc` on the same kept native stack, this update leaves `flow` and `replies` active. The latter spec's `activateOkrGroup()` requires the exact state `flow=false,okr=true,replies=false`, so it aborts before exercising its journey. Add failure-safe teardown that restores the groups changed by this spec.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Exclude stale candidates from the M2 delivery assertion**

Under Playwright `--retries`, or a second invocation after an attempt failed after creating candidates but before acknowledging them, Ben still has pending alerts from the earlier attempt. The desktop fetches those alerts too, and `recorded().slice(before)` therefore contains IDs outside the newly built `expected` array, making this exact equality fail even when the current attempt behaves correctly. Retire prior pending candidates or otherwise isolate the delivery queue before opening the desktop.

Right, and intended: this PR's own tree has no M2 client, so the click journey cannot pass from it alone. It depends on #4023 (TXE-4672: `CLIENT_GROUPS = ['okr','flow','replies']` plus the desktop proxy forwarding `X-OKR-Notification-Groups`, at 1b0357298). This PR is not merged before #4023.

Addressed in 90a7cf6f3: the spec now checks `CLIENT_GROUPS` first and stops with "this build must declare the flow and replies groups (TXE-4672)" rather than failing at the first click. The spec is skipped everywhere except the native harness (`OKR_NC_DESKTOP_M2=1`).

Evidence: on a composition with #4023 at c1012bd56 the first click stopped at update_required (the proxy defect, since fixed in 1b0357298); on the composition with 1b0357298 (0aa66512c) the full journey passed, run n2.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Restore Ben's alert preferences after both specs**

On a kept database, this write permanently disables Ben's quiet hours—and creates a saved-preferences row when `prefs.saved` was false—because the failure-safe teardown restores only source groups. The OS spec performs the same mutation, so a later spec in the shared run observes settings left by whichever spec ran first; snapshot and restore the original preferences (including removing a newly inserted row) in teardown.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Retire stale alerts before opening the OS notifier**

On a retry or second run against a kept database, an earlier attempt can have failed after creating a candidate but before the desktop fetched it. This initial `open()` immediately fetches such pending alerts before the new warm-up candidate is created, so macOS can show multiple indistinguishable Flow banners and the person may click an old one, invalidating the advertised single-notification journey. Settle existing pending candidates or otherwise isolate the queue before launching the real notifier.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Restore rows changed by stale-alert cleanup**

When this runs on a kept database after a partial or failed NC attempt, `/read-all` marks every visible unread notification belonging to Ben as read and increments its version, including rows this spec did not create. The `afterAll` teardown restores only source groups and preferences, so a later retry or NC spec observes the earlier attempt's inbox permanently altered. Snapshot and restore those rows, or isolate stale alert candidates without changing unrelated inbox state.
